exact_statement: For n>=2, the probability law q on subsets of [n] with q({i})=1/n has Shannon entropy ln(n) and expected subset size 1. Hence no universal C bounds entropy by C times expected size for all subset laws. This law is not the squared Fourier spectrum of any Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}.
assumptions: Uniform measure on the Boolean cube
All spectral mass on singleton sets
proof: The entropy and mean size are immediate. Any real Fourier expansion with this law is f(x)=sum_i a_i x_i with |a_i|=1/sqrt(n). Booleanity requires f(x)^2=1 identically. Its {i,j} Fourier coefficient is 2a_i a_j, nonzero for distinct i,j, a contradiction.
counterexample_scope: Refutes the bridge from an arbitrary subset probability law's expected size to entropy. Does not refute FEI for Boolean spectra.
remaining_gap: Find and audit a Boolean-specific premise that excludes this law and suffices for a dimension-free entropy bound.

exact_statement: For every even n=2m>=4, let g(x)=product_{j=1}^m(1+x_{2j-1}+x_{2j}-x_{2j-1}x_{2j})/2, y=(1,...,1), h=g-2*1{x=y}, and F(x,t)=g(x)-(1-t)*1{x=y}. Under uniform measure and base-2 Fourier entropy, I_t(F)=2^{-n} and H(F)-(H(g)+H(h))/2 >= n*2^{-n}. Thus a universal entropy-increment bound for every Boolean function and every coordinate is false.
proof: All g coefficients equal +/-r, r=2^{-n/2}, with plus fraction (1+r)/2. Put p=r^2 and L(u)=((1+r)/2)phi(1-ur)+((1-r)/2)phi(1+ur), phi(z)=z^2 log_2(z^2). Direct spectral accounting gives Delta_t=np+L(2)/2-L(1), I_t=p. On u in [0,2], arguments of phi lie in [1/2,3/2]; phi''(z)=(4 ln z+6)/ln2>0. Hence L(1)<=L(2)/2. See full proof artifact.
remaining_gap: Does not refute existence of a function-dependent good splitting coordinate; that is the remaining induction bridge.

exact_statement: For every even n>=4, the Boolean F(x,t)=g(x)-(1-t)1{x=(1,...,1)} from C002 satisfies H(F)<=2I(F), where I(F)=n/2+(n+1)2^{-n}. Thus the unbounded bad-coordinate increment ratio in C002 does not contradict FEI.
assumptions: The explicit disjoint-pair core g from C002
proof: Each core-coordinate influence is 1/2+p, p=2^{-n}; the selector influence is p. Spectral entropy conditioned on selector membership is at most n, hence H(F)<=n+h_2(p)<=n+(n+2)p<=2I(F). See BENT_SELECTOR.md.
remaining_gap: Only this explicit family; does not imply general FEI or the existential coordinate bridge.

exact_statement: For every Boolean f on a uniform d-cube and every coordinate i, put p=I_i(f) and Delta_i=H(f)-(H(f|i=+1)+H(f|i=-1))/2, using base-2 entropy. Then 0<=Delta_i<=h_2(p)+(2/ln2)p<=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln2)p, with zero conventions. Furthermore sup_{d,f,i:p>0}[Delta_i/p-log_2(1/p)]=3/ln2.
assumptions: All coordinates, not an existential choice
proof: Grouping paired Fourier coefficients gives Delta_i=JS_2(a^2,b^2)+sum_S m_S h_2(q_S). Concavity bounds the second term by h_2(p). A scalar derivative proof gives JS_e(P,Q)<=sum(sqrt(P)-sqrt(Q))^2/2, hence JS_2(a^2,b^2)<=2p/ln2. The explicit C002 witnesses satisfy Delta_t/p-log_2(1/p)->3/ln2 by a uniform Taylor expansion. Full proof, endpoints and sign factors are in SHARP_COORDINATE_BOUND.md.
remaining_gap: Full author derivation awaits independent check; this bound diverges as p decreases and does not resolve the existential coordinate step.
numerical_evidence: sharpness_measurements.json: 6 bounded high-precision diagnostics; finite checks are not the limit proof

exact_statement: Fix 0<tau<1. General FEI is equivalent to a bound H(f)<=C_tau I(f) for all Boolean functions whose coordinate influences are all <tau, with C_tau independent of dimension. The restricted-class bound implies general FEI with constant max(C_tau,log_2(1/tau)+3/ln2).
assumptions: A fixed tau independent of dimension
The assumed low-influence estimate covers every dimension and every Boolean function in that class

source.type: owner-own-work (separate derivation of an existing brain lead)

proof: Split at a coordinate with influence >=tau until every coordinate influence is <tau. The tree terminates because dimension decreases. Apply C004's coordinate bound and I(f)=(I(g)+I(h))/2+I_i(f) at branching nodes, and the assumed C_tau bound at leaves. Induction yields the maximum constant. The converse follows by restricting the universal FEI quantifiers.
remaining_gap: No dimension-free bound for the assumed low-influence class is established. This is a reduction, not a solution.
novelty: not new; rederived component of existing provisional brain card

exact_statement: For a nonconstant Boolean f under uniform cube measure, define delta=max_i I_i(f)>0 and rho_0(f)=min_{i:I_i(f)>0} Delta_i(f)/I_i(f), with base-2 Fourier entropy increment. Then rho_0(f)<=(1+h_2(delta))/delta. Reading delta as uniform input-coordinate bias makes that assertion false: AND_3 has rho_0=3+(9/4)log_2(16/9)>4 although every input coordinate has bias 1/2.
assumptions: delta is maximal flip influence, not input bias
proof: Delta_i=JS_2+B_i<=1+h_2(I_i). Choose a maximal-influence coordinate and use the minimum defining rho_0. AND_3's Fourier atom masses 9/16 and seven copies of 1/16, with child average entropy 1 and influence 1/4, give the exact counterexample to the input-bias reading.
